resources.string: Enter your clinometer readings to instantly get the tree\'s height.
Please enter a valid distance (greater than 0 meters)
Please enter a valid top angle
Please enter a valid bottom angle
Height is measured using the two-angle clinometer formula:

1. Measure the horizontal distance from your position to the tree.
2. Aim the clinometer upward at the treetop and record the top angle.
3. Aim the clinometer upward at the tree base too, and record the bottom angle.
4. The result is the tree's height in meters.

string-array.name: hint_tip_titles
string-array.item: Leaning Tree? Stand to the Side

string-array.name: hint_tip_descriptions
string-array.item: This formula needs a straight, horizontal distance to the tree — not a slanted distance that follows the ground\'s slope.
This formula works when the tree base is lower than your eye level (both angles are aimed upward).
If the distance follows the ground\'s slope (slope distance), the calculated tree height may come out taller than it actually is.
Stand to the side of the tree, not in front of or behind its lean, for a more accurate reading.
Ideally, stand at a distance roughly equal to the tree\'s height. For a ~15-20m tree, stand 15-20m away too.
This formula is for trees at least 2 meters tall. For anything shorter, just measure it directly without a clinometer.
